design.md's ## ADR Change Log (lines 177-181) states 'None ... proposes no ADR revision' and cites only ADR-0019 (docs/adr/0019-approval-sidecar-protection.md, confirmed to exist on disk) as a read-only authoritative source -- but ADR-0019 is the hook-activation-handshake defense-claim ADR this feature's live-host proof discharges, not an ADR for the new cryptographic mechanism design.md itself introduces: an Ed25519 digital-signature scheme with a maintainer-committed a8-trusted-signers.json public-key/role registry, a signed nonce-issuance ledger, and domain-separated signing targets (Data Plan 'Signing Contract' section, lines 572-604; Components table line 104, a8-trusted-signers.json; line 101, nonce-ledger.json). No prior use of Ed25519/public-key signing was found anywhere else in this repository (grep -rli 'ed25519|digital signature|public.key|private.key' across docs/, plugins/, scripts/, tests/ returns no genuinely related hits outside this feature's own spec). This repository's own ADR practice already treats a comparably-scoped decision -- who is permitted to perform cryptographic signature verification and where -- as ADR-level material: ADR-0008 (docs/adr/0008-evidence-deep-verify-no-signature-crypto.md) scopes a deliberate no-signature-verification decision to the sdd-forge-mcp evidence_deep_verify tool and states that any component newly performing signature verification requires 'this ADR's supersession and a new security review' (ADR-0008 Consequences, line 48-49). design.md introduces a new, repository-first signing/key-trust mechanism without listing or proposing a new ADR for it.
